text:
Panagbenga Festival (Flower Festival) is a month-long annual flower festival occurring in the city of pines—Baguio.
The term is of Malayo-Polynesian origin, meaning "season of blooming".
The festival, held during the month of February, was created as a tribute to the city's flowers and as a way to rise up from the devastation of the 1990 Luzon earthquake.
Dark red for strawberries and vivid yellow for sunflowers—these were just some of the colors that stood out during Panagbenga 2017's Grand Street Parade.
Select elementary and high school students performed before a sea of festivalgoers on the city's busiest streets.
Flowers were, of course, the most dominant element of the parade.
Some groups, however, chose to wear costumes that featured the city’s most popular products, such as woven baskets, strawberries, and “walis tambo” or brooms made of local plant materials.
Beyond a bright spectrum of colors, the performances also highlighted Cordillera’s rich culture—from ethnic music to traditional dances. Some groups performed “tayaw,” a popular Cordillera dance routine, while others imitated the cañao, a dance ritual Cordillerans perform on sacred occasions.
Kalinga tattoos, as popularized by Apo Whang-Od, and colorful textiles from different indigenous groups in Northern Philippines were also highlighted.
Noticeably, some performers wore costumes that imitated the wings of bees and butterflies, paying tribute to the pollinators that keep the city’s flower industry vibrant.

M Lhuillier continues to offer non-stop activities this year as they open the "Spot the ML Panagbenga Float" photo contest to all hobbyist, amateur, and professional photographers who will be present to witness and capture the moments of Panagbenga Festival 2020 Grand Parade this March 1 in Baguio City. ▫
Here are the guidelines of the contest:
1. The photo must depict the ML FLOAT as it traverses the usual Panagbenga parade route. Maximum of three entries will be given for each participant.
2. Photo must be in digital format.
3. Only global manipulation is allowed in this contest.
4. Watermarks and other identifying marks are not allowed. 
5. Official entries must be in 8”x10”, 300dpi, colored prints without borders. 
6. Each photo entry must be labeled with the participants’ mobile numbers only 
7. Soft copies of the RAW and edited files must be submitted through email at clau.clarin@mlhuillier.com
8. Participant must include their contact number, email, and Facebook name during the submission of entries. 
9. Participants must allow the organizers to freely use their entries for promotional purposes. The photographer will be properly credited or acknowledged on each image used. 
10. Winners will be notified by phone, e-mail, or Facebook. 
11. Current employees of M Lhuillier Financial Services Inc. and their relatives up to the 2nd degree of consanguinity, its suppliers, digital services providers and advertising agency and affinity are disqualified to join the photo contest. ▫
Criteria for Judging
a) Visual Impact/Overall Impression - 20% 
b) Creativity - 30% 
c) Composition - 20% 
d) Technical Quality - 30% ▫
Winners will receive the following prizes: 
1st Prize- P 5,000.00 
2nd Prize-P 3,000.00 
3rd Prize- P 2,000.00 
4TH to 10th Finalist will be given a certificate ▫
The deadline for the submission of entries will be on March 10, 2020 at 3:00pm.
▫
Wishing all the participants good luck!

This coming April 2-3, 2022 marks the holding of the first moto festival in the flower festival's history. Aptly named 'Bikes in Bloom', the event aims to reinvigorate Panagbenga’s tradition of showcasing Baguio’s flowers in a fun and safe way. By inviting various riders, highlighting women, to spruce-up their 2-wheeled vehicles (motorcycles, bicycles, scooters) with fresh flowers. These riders will roam around Baguio’s cafes and restaurants to promote MotoTourism and advocate women empowerment as March is also Women’s Month. With this year’s theme “Let Hope Bloom,” the idea is to revive Panagbenga and have an alternative and new way to parade the flowers around the City in place of the usual Street Dancing and Float Parade.

In support of the celebration of Panagbenga 2022 (Special Edition), the Department of Tourism-CAR in partnership with the City of Baguio, Baguio Flower Festival Inc. (BFFI), and the Boatmen Association of Burnham Park will be staging a Fluvial Float Parade on March 26, 2022 from 9:00am- 11:00am at the Burnham Lake.

the ilocano word for usbong in Filipino or sprout in English, was chosen to represent this exhibition as we emerge from 2years of isolation.

text:
Session road in Bloom 2023

Another highlight of Baguio's Flower festival is the Session Road in bloom. From my understanding its an exposition of different products of Baguio and other provinces in the Philippines ranging from food, hand crafted items, to thrift shops and a showcase of differnt Baguio talents from music, dance, and even actual art and others. 

After 2 years of not experiencing the festivities of Panagbenga, people from near and far came to enjoy its higlights. Considering that this photo was taken on a weekday we can safely assume that the festive spirit is pretty much alive and will probably grow through the days or even the years.

Thanks to @ashotofbaguio for inviting me on this photo walk I have enjoyed being on the streets again taking pictures of the fun and chaos of Panagbenga and I have most enjoyed your company ^_^

It was Zion's first long bus ride and we had a blast! 

📍 Northern Blossom Flower Farm in Atok, Benguet

🚸 Child-friendliness Rating: 6/10
▶️ It's a beautiful, heavenly place but it could use some additional railings or fences especially on areas where there are steep drops. It's like flower terraces (instead of rice terraces) so I'm not sure if adding fences at the edges will affect the plant growth. But for me, it doesn't feel safe. I never let Zion walk alone on his own during this entire tour for about 2 hours because one wrong step and he'll fall down the next level! ENTRANCE FEE is 250+50 environmental fee

▶️ And don't even get me started about the commute to the place! Zion was sleeping so good for him, but for me, I almost vomited and I NEVER get nauseous on any rides all my life! text:
‘Panagbenga’ here in Baguio is known as the month-long celebration of Cordillera’s culture and heritage: where people flock to watch a showcase of dance performances, flower floats, artisan markets, among many others. 

The term is of ‘Kanankaey’ origin, a south central Cordilleran language, which means, ‘the season for blooming’.

As for its history, the festival was born in 1996 as a way to boost morale and tourism after the devastating earthquake that hit Luzon in 1990. The festival has been postponed during the pandemic and now it is back in full swing in joyous northern celebration for better things ahead. We see the streets are once again filled with song and color. 

Panagbenga is not just an annual tourist attraction of flora and fauna. In careful thought, it is a moving garden of stories that speaks of the resilience of this city and its people, and the hope that every bloom brings. 🌸

Seen during the Panagbenga Festival Street Dancing event held in Baguio City, some 250 kms. north of Manila, on 25 February 2023.

Panagbenga is an annual flower festival celebrated every February which takes place in Baguio City, Philippines. 

The term “Panagbenga” comes from a Kankanaey term meaning “season of blooming”. 

This festival reflects the history, traditions and values of Baguio and the Cordilleras. It lasts over a month long and flourishes through community spirit involvement.

Why does the sunflower bloom?

Sunflowers are faithful,
they delight in warm kisses
and wilt in its absence;
they tower above tulips, yet,
look expectingly skyward
—awaiting the radiant sun.

Sunflowers are joyful,
they brighten in daylight
and gleefully celebrate
every new morning dew,
unapologetically,
unconditionally.

And every sunset,
the yellow blooms wait
for next light’s glow
even when it rains,
even when it hides
—the sun’s flower hopes.

And so,
they wait,
they smile,
they hope,
they bloom
—they love.

The sunflower blooms.

By Jezreel Cayat
Illustration by Ashley Trajano

Baguio City came alive last February 23, as the Panagbenga Festival’s Grand Floral Float Parade, themed "Blossom Beyond Boundaries," brightened the streets with stunning flower displays, lively performances, and a vibrant crowd along Session Road.

The parade, which began at 8:00 AM, made its way from Upper Session Road to the Melvin Jones Grandstand, filling the air with the beauty of nature and creativity. The spirit of Panagbenga touched every corner of the city, uniting people across all boundaries.

text:
My last visit to Baguio Botanical Garden was ages ago, so I was surprised to see the changes brought about by renovations made during the pandemic. 

The garden is now more appealing to tourists that are looking for Instagrammable photo opportunities because every turn leads to a wonderful backdrop of flowers such as dahlias, sunflowers, daisies, and orchids of various types. 

There is also a mix of garden themes (can be confusing at first, but just enjoy the stroll inside) symbolizing friendships forged between countries such as the United States, Japan, South Korea, Thailand, China, and Canada.

The Botanical Garden also has outdoor galleries and art installations set up by the Baguio Arts Guild, a WWII tunnel dug by the Japanese, plant stores and small cafes. 

Even with the new aesthetics of snaking pathways, ramps, and waving gardens, the old mock-up Cordilleran village still remains, and visitors can still get their photo taken in traditional Igorot clothing. 

It may be because of the #Panagbenga2025 weekend, but I'm glad to see the Botanical Garden becoming a tourism draw again.

The Panagbenga Festival 2025 is Baguio City's annual flower festival, celebrated every February. The festival's name, "Panagbenga," means "season of blooming" in the Kankanaey language. This year, the theme is "Blossoms Beyond Boundaries".

The festival features a month-long celebration filled with grand parades, cultural performances, and colorful floral displays. Some of the key events include:

- Grand Opening Day Parade: February 1, 2025
- Panagbengascapes Landscaping Competition and Exhibition: February 1 - March 2, 2025
- Grand Street Dance Parade: February 22, 2025
- Grand Floral Float Parade: February 23, 2025
- Session Road in Bloom: February 24 - March 2, 2025
- Fluvial Parade: February 27, 2025
- Closing and Awarding Ceremonies: March 2, 2025
- Grand Aerial Fireworks Display: March 2, 2025

The Panagbenga Festival is a celebration of Baguio's floral beauty and the rich culture and traditions of the Cordilleran people. It's one of the most anticipated festivals in the Philippines, attracting both locals and tourists alike.

text:
Ang Panagbenga Festival ay isang taunang pagdiriwang sa Baguio City na ginaganap tuwing Pebrero. Kilala ito bilang "Flower Festival" dahil  ipinapakita nito ang kagandahan ng mga bulaklak sa pamamagitan ng mga makukulay na parada ng float na puno ng bulaklak at mga street dance na may temang bulaklak.

#Panagbenga2025 
#baguioflowerparade 
#streetdance 
Clarisse Ferfas
Ang Panagbenga ay nagmula sa salitang Kankanaey na nangangahulugang "season of blooming" o panahon ng pamumulaklak. Nagsimula ito noong 1996 upang ipakita ang kultura ng Cordillera at pasiglahin ang turismo sa Baguio matapos ang lindol noong 1990.

Bukod sa parada, may iba pang mga aktibidad tulad ng Session Road in Bloom (isang street market at food fair), fireworks display, at iba't ibang paligsahan. Isa ito sa pinaka-aabangan at pinakamalaking festival sa Pilipinas.

An unforgettable moment for Narvacan! This year, we proudly made our debut in the Grand Float Parade during the Panagbenga Festival 2025, showcasing a beautiful tribute to our rich history🌻

Our float depicted a symbol of our rich history and the legendary origin of how Narvacan got its name, referencing the captivating story of the Spanish ship through stunning flower arrangements. 💐

Our float was graced by none other than @krishnahgravidez , Miss World Philippines 2025 and Susan Sanidad, the First Lady of Narvacan. 🌹

A heartfelt thank you to Krishnah for representing our hometown with such grace and charm! Your dedication and passion in representing the Philippines inspire us all. As you prepare for the Miss World competition, know that our community stands behind you, cheering you on every step of the way. 🇵🇭

Let’s continue to celebrate the beauty of our culture, the vibrant spirit of our community, and the journey ahead! 🌸 

📖 How Narvacan Got Its Name 📖

Narvacan’s name is rooted in a legendary Spanish expedition. In 1576, Don Juan de Salcedo sent a ship south from Vigan, but a fierce storm struck, forcing the vessel against the rocky shores near the Santa-Narvacan boundary. It drifted south and capsized in Camantirisan, now Pantoc.

As the locals rescued the Spanish survivors, a misunderstanding arose. When asked, “Nalbaka? Nalbakayo?” the Spaniards mistook it for the place’s name, recording it as Nalvacan—which later became Narvacan. ⚓️

text:
If there’s one thing I’ve learned in this motherhood journey, it’s that food is our love language. And because we all know yung traffic sa Baguio and at this time ayaw na namin lumabas ng CJH. I searched kung ano yung mga pwedeng puntahan na breakfast spot inside. I saw Hill Station Bistro. Maliit lang yung space pero masasabi namin na kumportable makakakain and they also have al fresco area but we opted inside nalang because it was very cold outside - agad lalamig yung food hehe. 

Our Breakfast served with coffee or tea and fresh fruits:
☀️The Exotic: Tapang Usa & Baboy Damo (for me and daddy jayr)
☀️The Classics: Baguio Longganisa & Country Breakfast Bacon (hati daw kami sa longganisa and country breakfast for R3)
☀️The Treat: Stuffed French Toast (for Rinoa)

The best part? Hindi siya kasing pricey as I expected! Reasonable ang pricelist for the quality and the vibe. Truth is, masarap lahat ng inorder namin. Walang tapon. Walang natira 😆

It’s rare for us to try foods like these regularly, kaya when we travel, we really make it a point to explore. It’s all about the balance - gastos today, tipid tomorrow 😅 Kahit busy sa pagiging mommy, importanteng ma-enjoy din natin ‘yung mga ganitong moment with the fam. Thankful ako sa husband ko kasi siya yung nag iintroduce sakin ng mga ganitong food. Picky eater momma here kaya di ko kinarir ang pagiging food vlogger. Haha! Sa susunod, Slaughterhaws naman daw kame pag okay na talaga paa niya, mga bawal lahat saknya dun eh. Haha! Yun lang, see you on my next post! (Ginawang voice over vlog 😂)

They say Panagbenga is a festival of color. This weekend, I’m proving it’s a festival of light.

I’m headed up to Baguio for Panagbenga 2026, but my bag is looking a little different this year. No color presets, no film simulations—just pure luminance. I’m field-testing the new Ricoh GR IV Monochrome, generously lent to me by Camerahaus (the official home of Pentax and GR in the PH).

While everyone is chasing the bright petals of the floats, I’ll be hunting for the textures, the deep shadows, and the raw energy that only a dedicated monochrome sensor can reveal.

text:
Color meets contrast this Panagbenga weekend.

The GR IV Monochrome 28mm and the GR iiix HDF 40mm (color) are ready for the streets of Baguio — two different sensors, two different visual philosophies, one flower festival.

Panagbenga is all about explosive hues — and that’s where the GR iiix HDF shines. The 40mm gives me that natural perspective compression, isolating dancers, details, and Sunday’s grand float highlights with beautiful color depth. Engage HDF, and the highlights bloom subtly — perfect for sunlit petals and reflective costumes.

Then there’s the GR Monochrome. No color. No distraction. Just pure tonality. It translates the spectacle into texture, contrast, and emotion — carving light from shadow, turning layered parades into graphic compositions.

28mm pulls me into the chaos.
40mm refines the story.

Black and white for mood.
Color for celebration.

Panagbenga 2026 — let’s work.

text:
Baguio light hits different through the HDF.
📷: © Edwin Tuyay Images
Taking the Ricoh GR IIIx HDF to Panagbenga 2026 was a game changer. No bulky bags, no lens swaps—just pure, candid moments. By toggling between the native 40mm for the streets and the 50mm/71mm crop modes for the floats, I felt like I had a full bag of primes in the palm of my hand.

The Highlight Diffusion Filter (HDF) was the secret sauce here, turning the sharp Baguio sun into a soft, cinematic glow. 🌸☁️

My 3 Festival Tips for the Gram:

 Go Stealth: Use a small camera to blend in. People act more natural when they don’t see a giant lens pointed at them.

 The Power of the Crop: Don't be afraid of digital crop modes! The 71mm on this sensor still delivers incredible sharpness with a beautiful tight perspective.

 Embrace the Glow: If the sun is harsh, use a diffusion filter (or the HDF) to soften the "digital" edge and give your shots a filmic soul.

text:
Breakthrough Purity That Honors God
By Sis. Jennifer Manlolo Luarca Ydia
📖 “Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.” – Matthew 5:8

Last Sunday, February 15, in the middle of the vibrant colors and celebrations of the Panagbenga Festival, we chose to begin our journey differently.

Before heading up to the cool heights of Atok, Benguet and continuing our Upper Northern Luzon vacation, we first went to the House of the Lord — JIL Baguio City.

While the city bloomed with flowers, God chose to bloom something deeper in our hearts.

The message was clear and piercing: Breakthrough begins with purity.

Sis. Jennilyn Ydia reminded us that purity is not perfection — it is alignment.

1️⃣ Purity Begins in the Heart
Before breakthrough manifests externally, it is cultivated internally. Our motives. Our thoughts. Our intentions before God. True purity is unseen by people but fully known by Him.

2️⃣ Purity Shapes Our Conduct
What fills the heart eventually flows into action. Our words, leadership, business dealings, relationships — all become reflections of what we allow God to cleanse and refine within us.

3️⃣ Purity in Calling — Living Out the Mission
Breakthrough is not just about personal victory. It is about living the mission God entrusted to us. Purity protects calling. Purity sustains impact. Purity honors God in success.

As tourists enjoyed the festival, we received a divine reminder:
Real breakthrough is not elevation in position — it is elevation in character.

And perhaps that was the greatest blessing of the trip.

Before the scenic views of Atok…
Before the mountain roads…
Before the rest and adventure…

God reminded us:
Keep the heart pure. Breakthrough will follow.

Grateful for the Word.
Grateful for the reminder.
Grateful that even on vacation, God speaks.

🥢 The Cozy Bowl - For ramen lovers who don't want to risk 500+ PHP for a single bowl. Plus points for their honesty -  they're not 100% authentic Japanese and they know how to listen to their customers. 

🥤 Donya Brewha (Hole In The Wall Cafe) - The concept of how they serve drinks is clever but cute. Tried their starters Honey Lemonade and Biscoff on two separate days, and it didn't disappoint me. 

🥪 Shiraz Smokehaus - You know when it's Erwan Heussaff who drop recos, rest assure that it is exceptionally safe and is truly something we can be proud of. Shiraz is one of them.

Did I missed something? If so, I'll try again next year...

Panagbenga Festival, Baguio 
Panagbenga Festival is a month-long annual flower festival occurring in Baguio. 
The term is of Kankanaey origin, meaning "season of blooming". The festival, held in February, was created as a tribute to the city's flowers and to rise from the devastation of the 1990 Luzon earthquake. Several activities are done during the festival which includes the parade floats covered mostly with flowers and street dancing, presented by dancers clad in flower-inspired costumes. The festival is also another way for people to rediscover the culture and old traditions of the ethnic groups came from Cordillera region. 
Photo by: Venus C. Lopez

The Panagbenga Festival is a month-long flower festival held in Baguio every year. This term is from Kankanaey origin, meaning "season of blooming." The festival, which takes place every February, was created as a tribute to the city's flowers and as a way to recover from the devastation caused by the 1990 Luzon earthquake. It also includes street dancing, which is inspired by the Bendian, an Ibaloi dance of celebration that originated in the Cordilleras. It also highlights the Cordilleras' rich culture and tradition, as well as our ancestors' heritage, which each Cordilleran is proud of.

text:
The Panagbenga Flower Festival from Baguio City, represented by The University of Cordilleras Center for Creative Productions, celebrated as runner-up and awarded the Pride of Place Award at Aliwan Fiesta 2024, highlighted the city's rich floral heritage. Known for its spectacular parade of floats adorned with colorful blooms, the festival captivated audiences with cultural dances and music that reflect the spirit of the Cordillera region. The event not only promotes tourism but also honors Baguio's commitment to environmental conservation and community unity. Panagbenga continues to be a cherished symbol of beauty and cultural pride in the Philippines.

CITY'S PANAGBENGA FLOAT A TRIBUTE TO SISTER CITIES

"Blossoms Beyond Boundaries."

The city government channels the Panagbenga theme in its float this year to symbolize the blossoming socio-economic partnerships established by the city with its international sister cities.

That it is a cross-border symbiotic relations that truly manifest how our own blossoms (city attributes and characteristics) can contribute and make impact to the world and vice versa.

The float will have flowers representing our city and our sister cities in 5 countries:
⚘ Everlasting/Sunflower - Baguio City, Philippines
⚘ Blue Bonnet - San Antonio Texas, USA
⚘ California Poppy/Rose - Vallejo California, USA
⚘ Yellow Hibiscus - Honolulu Hawaii , USA
⚘ Mugunghwa - Taebaek and Gongju Cities, Korea
⚘ Cherry Blossom - Hanyu City, Japan
⚘ Plum Blossom/Peony - Hangzhou, China
⚘ Bunchberry - Vaughan City Ontario, Canada
...accompanied by our beauty queens donning traditional national attires of the different countries.

Design concept rendering by Ar. Elaine Ganga and float construction by City Buildings and Architecture Office

text:
An unforgettable moment for Narvacan! This year, we proudly made our debut in the Grand Float Parade during the Panagbenga Festival 2025, showcasing a beautiful tribute to our rich history🌻

Our float depicted a symbol of our rich history and the legendary origin of how Narvacan got its name, referencing the captivating story of the Spanish ship through stunning flower arrangements. 💐

Our float was graced by none other than @krishnahgravidez , Miss World Philippines 2025 and Susan Sanidad, the First Lady of Narvacan. 🌹

A heartfelt thank you to Krishnah for representing our hometown with such grace and charm! Your dedication and passion in representing the Philippines inspire us all. As you prepare for the Miss World competition, know that our community stands behind you, cheering you on every step of the way. 🇵🇭

Let’s continue to celebrate the beauty of our culture, the vibrant spirit of our community, and the journey ahead! 🌸 

📖 How Narvacan Got Its Name 📖

Narvacan’s name is rooted in a legendary Spanish expedition. In 1576, Don Juan de Salcedo sent a ship south from Vigan, but a fierce storm struck, forcing the vessel against the rocky shores near the Santa-Narvacan boundary. It drifted south and capsized in Camantirisan, now Pantoc.

As the locals rescued the Spanish survivors, a misunderstanding arose. When asked, “Nalbaka? Nalbakayo?” the Spaniards mistook it for the place’s name, recording it as Nalvacan—which later became Narvacan. ⚓️

Blooming Weaves: A Stunning Showcase of Cordilleran Fashion at SM City Baguio

The Blooming Weaves: Panagbenga Fashion Show & Exhibit 2025 brought an explosion of color, culture, and creativity to SM City Baguio on February 21. Set against the vibrant backdrop of Panagbenga Festival, this spectacular runway event celebrated the artistry of Cordilleran weaving and modern fashion.

Featuring visionary designers like Eros Goze, Andrew Visaya Jr., Julienne Paran, Lhee Wel Tokia, Muquiat Padong, Ayra Longsiab, Radley Calderon, Genesis Gonzales, Avelyn Calag, and Mariz Bomogao, the show redefined indigenous textiles with contemporary elegance. The runway dazzled with intricate designs, bold silhouettes, and a deep appreciation for heritage woven into every piece.

Adding to the grandeur, the Gawis Culture and Arts Ensemble delivered a mesmerizing performance, further immersing the audience in the spirit of Cordilleran artistry.
